title: Redwood Discovery - Migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery to evaluate migrating OrionX inference from OpenAI hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated/Private. Covered compatibility with vLLM/TGI, model and quantization support, eval parity, perf expectations, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and a proposed POC/benchmark plan.
topics: Networking and security requirements (VPC, KMS, SSO)
action_items: Jordan Park: Share Dedicated pricing tiers and committed options (due: 2026-11-09)
Maya Singh: Send benchmark checklist and sample eval harness (due: 2026-11-08)
Priya Patel: Provide list of models, current QPS, and token distribution (due: 2026-11-10)
Sofia Alvarez: Send security specific requirements and any compliance docs needed (due: 2026-11-12)
Marco Ruiz: Prep a small dataset of 200 prompts for parity tests (due: 2026-11-11)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing + Dedicated architecture diagram
Schedule a 60-minute benchmark setup session week of 11/15
Kick off 2-week pilot using Redwood Dedicated with one reserved GPU pool
Exchange security docs (SOC2 report, SAML/SSO integration steps, KMS/HSM options)
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2026-11-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE); Liam Chen (CTO, OrionX), Priya Patel (Head of Platform), Marco Ruiz (ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Security)

[00:12] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood. Quick intro, we'll run through a few questions to understand your migration goals, then Maya will cover technical compatibility and benchmarks.

[00:25] Liam Chen: Hi, thanks. Quick context — we've been on OpenAI for 18 months, mostly chat completions and embeddings. Cost's spiking and we need lower latencies for serving agent flows. Also, compliance wants more control over deployments.

[00:40] Maya Singh: Great, that tracks with a lot of folks. Can you tell us current QPS and latency targets? Also which models you're running and whether you're using vLLM or TGI internally?

[00:55] Priya Patel: We're about 120 QPS peak across a few endpoints, avg request ~250 tokens, 95th p95 latency target for user-facing is under 400ms. We're using GPT-4 style 8k-ish context models from OpenAI; for on-prem tests we've tried running vLLM with LlamaX-8B and TGI for some custom quantized weights.

[01:20] Maya Singh: Okay, perfect. So two threads — 1) migration to Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and 2) potential Private/VPC for compliance. On compatibility: Redwood's serving supports model formats we commonly see — Hugging Face, ONNX, GGML-derived quantized checkpoints — and we have specific kernel paths for int8 and int4 quantized runs. When you say TGI/vLLM, are you running custom conversion pipelines?

[01:46] Marco Ruiz: We convert weights ourselves with a mix of bitsandbytes and some custom scripts; latency looks good in vLLM but we see throughput issues at scale. Concern is eval parity — we don't want subtle deltas in completions when switching runtime.

[02:05] Ethan Wu: Right, eval parity is a big one. Our usual approach is to run your eval suite across both endpoints: current OpenAI baseline, your vLLM/TGI internal baseline, and Redwood Dedicated baseline. We instrument tokens, sampling seeds where applicable, and compare logprobs and output similarity metrics. Small paraphrase differences are expected, but major deltas we can trace to tokenizer or sampling differences.

[02:35] Sofia Alvarez: From security, we need VPC peering or private networking, KMS for keys (HSM if possible), audit logs for all inference requests, and SOC2 or equivalent reports. Also data residency in AWS eu-west-1 for our EU customers.

[02:55] Jordan Park: That makes sense. Redwood Private supports customer-controlled VPCs, KMS integration, and we provide audit logs and retention controls. Our SOC2 and ISO artifacts can be shared — we'll add that to next steps.

[03:15] Liam Chen: How do you handle model rollout — can we do canary/percentage rollouts between OpenAI and Dedicated, or stay on Redwood Dedicated and fallback to OpenAI?

[03:27] Maya Singh: We support smart routing. You can route by latency or cost; fallback to hosted if Dedicated has transient issues. We also support A/B and canary deployments per route so you can test on a subset before full migration.

[03:45] Priya Patel: About throughput — our current issue is spikes causing throttles. We need reserved GPU pools and autoscaling. What are Redwood Dedicated guarantees?

[03:57] Jordan Park: Dedicated provides reserved capacity options with SLA-backed throughput. We can provision a committed GPU pool sized to your peak with burst capacity. For the pilot we'd propose a small reserved pool sized for your baseline to validate and then plan scale.

[04:15] Marco Ruiz: Technical: when converting from our TGI pipeline, will Redwood's runtime respect the same sampling parameters? We observed different outputs when temperature/stateful sampling varied.

[04:28] Maya Singh: Yes, we surface the same sampling parameters — temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition_penalty — but small implementation differences can matter. We recommend fixing seeds during eval runs and aligning tokenizers. Also, ensure KV cache handling is equivalent — some runtimes truncate or re-encode prefix differently which can cause drift.

[04:55] Liam Chen: Any gotchas with quantization? We use int8 mostly but experimenting with int4 to save cost. vLLM supports a bunch of kernels; do you support those kernels or similar performance?

[05:10] Ethan Wu: We support int8 and optimized int4 execution paths; our kernel selection does model/sequence-length aware tuning. For int4 we recommend validating on your eval set — there can be tiny hallucination regressions with aggressive quant. We also can run mixed precision where critical tokens use higher precision.

[05:32] Priya Patel: Networking — can Redwood Dedicated sit in our AWS account or do we need to peering? We prefer deployment in our AWS account for log access.

[05:44] Jordan Park: For Private deployments we can run control plane in Redwood and data plane in your account (bring-your-own VPC). Dedicated hosted is multi-tenant but isolated; Private gives you full network control. For the pilot, BH (bring-hosted?) we usually do either a dedicated instance inside a partner VPC or a remote VPC peering setup — we'll send diagrams.

[06:05] Sofia Alvarez: About keys — do you offer CMEK (customer managed encryption keys)?

[06:11] Maya Singh: Yes, we integrate with KMS providers and can support CMEK. HSM-backed keys are an enterprise option.

[06:22] Marco Ruiz: On metrics: we need per-token latency breakdowns to debug hotspots. Does Redwood expose that?

[06:28] Ethan Wu: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level traces, per-route and per-model dashboards, and hooks for custom traces. We also provide exportable logs for downstream analysis.

[06:45] Liam Chen: Ok, pilot plan? What would you recommend to validate eval parity and performance?

[06:52] Maya Singh: Recommend three-step pilot: 1) parity eval — run your 200-500 prompt eval set on OpenAI and on Redwood Dedicated with same sampling seeds, compare outputs and logprobs; 2) perf baseline — synthetic load test to validate p95/p99 under your token distribution; 3) small production canary routing (5-10% traffic) for 1-2 weeks. We'll provide the benchmark harness and can support the load testing.

[07:22] Marco Ruiz: Do you require model weight handover, or can we point Redwood to an S3 bucket holding converted artifacts?

[07:30] Maya Singh: Either works. For Dedicated/Private you can upload model artifacts to a customer-controlled S3 with appropriate IAM. We have conversion tooling if you need help translating to the runtime-optimized format, but we don't require you to hand over training weights.

[07:45] Priya Patel: One concern — our current prompt engineering relies on OpenAI-specific behaviors. Will system prompts, function calls, and streaming behave the same?

[07:58] Ethan Wu: Function calling semantics and streaming are supported; there are subtle differences in function call heuristics across models. We'll help you map function call responses and provide a compatibility matrix for common OpenAI endpoints.

[08:15] Sofia Alvarez: Legal/compliance question — data retention and deletion requests, do you have a documented process?

[08:22] Jordan Park: Yes, we have data retention controls and documented deletion APIs; for Private deployments you have full control. We'll send the retention and deletion policy docs.

[08:35] Liam Chen: Pricing — rough ballpark per-token or per-reserved GPU cost?

[08:43] Jordan Park: For Dedicated it's a mix of reserved monthly capacity + per-token inference cost depending on model size/quant. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we see your model footprint and QPS. For the pilot we can offer a short-term evaluation rate.

[08:58] Priya Patel: How long to spin up a Dedicated cluster for pilot?

[09:03] Maya Singh: We can spin up a pilot cluster in 3-5 business days once we agree on sizing and network access. Private deployments take longer due to VPC onboarding, typically 2-4 weeks.

[09:17] Marco Ruiz: If we use our vLLM/TGI converted weights and then later want Redwood to host updated weights automatically, is there a CI flow?

[09:25] Ethan Wu: We have model registry APIs and CI integrations; you can push new artifacts to S3 and trigger redeploys, and we support version pinning and rollbacks.

[09:40] Liam Chen: Can we run a side-by-side A/B where the Dedicated path uses a quantized model and OpenAI uses full precision to compare quality/cost tradeoffs?

[09:49] Maya Singh: Absolutely. That's a common eval. We can help design experiments and metrics to measure quality degradation vs cost savings.

[10:05] Priya Patel: Ok, operational: who on Redwood will be our point for the pilot?

[10:10] Jordan Park: I'll be your AE lead, Maya will be the SE lead for the benchmark and onboarding, Ethan will help with infra and perf tuning.

[10:20] Sofia Alvarez: We'll need to schedule a technical deep dive with our security and infra folks before signing.

[10:27] Jordan Park: Sounds good; we'll propose a 60-minute deep dive next week focused on VPC/KMS/SSO and audit log schema.

[10:35] Liam Chen: Any documentation on compatibility with vLLM/TGI conversion steps?

[10:40] Maya Singh: Yes, we have a migration playbook that lists conversion examples, tokenizer checks, and sample scripts. We'll share that.

[10:49] Marco Ruiz: What about embeddings parity? We use embeddings heavily for search; OpenAI embeddings currently in production.

[10:56] Ethan Wu: Embeddings parity is tricky across models — we recommend running our embedding similarity eval. For some use cases you can host the same model weights for embeddings; other times you may choose a smaller dedicated embedder for cost. We'll include embedding eval in the pilot plan.

[11:15] Priya Patel: Monitoring/alerts — SLA breach alarms and cost alerts — can we hook into our PagerDuty?

[11:22] Jordan Park: Yes, Redwood Console supports webhook alerts, PagerDuty integrations, and cost anomaly detection.

[11:35] Jordan Park: I'll recap aloud. Redwood to send pricing, SOC2 and private deployment docs, benchmark harness, and architecture diagrams. OrionX to share model list, typical token distribution, and 200 prompt eval set. We'll schedule benchmark setup and a deep dive on security. Anything to add?

[11:55] Liam Chen: That covers it, thanks. One quick question — if we see minor eval regressions with int4 can Redwood help tune quant settings?

[12:04] Maya Singh: Yes, tuning quantization profiles is part of Redwood Optimize — we'll pair on that during the pilot.

[12:15] Jordan Park: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials by end of week.

[12:22] Meeting end.
